Seat broad purple double doors behind the reveal with seam, two handles, and a readable bee crest. No dark capsule, circular disk, or single thin backplane may define the portal.

Build the rose as an embedded cluster of recessed hexagonal tubes/cells inside the upper gable, not a circular plate or frame. It must be smaller and less contrast-heavy than the door and may never protrude beyond side silhouette.
Build four dominant front occupied bays as closed extruded honey-cell pods with real depth, side returns, dark recessed cells, low faceted roofs, and clear separation at 0, 45 and 315 degrees.
Build the hero crown from a closed polygonal drum plus a low faceted honeycomb-cage roof. Use structural hex ribs and an embedded amber core; do not use a tall smooth hemisphere or onion bulb.

Build four quadrant satellite towers as polygonal inhabited lanterns with visible honey-cell openings and low faceted cage roofs. Front pair frame the entrance; rear pair are shorter and simpler. Avoid equal-status perimeter domes.

Wrap ribs, eaves, window cells, buttresses and honey channels continuously around corners. All facade ornaments need thickness and attachment sockets; no surface may collapse into a shard at any 45-degree orbit.

Use wax-cream masonry, gold-bronze exoskeleton, dark occupied recesses, purple enamel and amber glass to recreate the exact source hierarchy. Honeycomb pattern must be visible in geometry and material response at phone scale.
Use selective viscous honey curtains and teardrops seated under eaves. Each drip requires an upper fillet/puddle, tapering stream and terminal drop; no lamp-post silhouette.
